High level ask: can you confirm the PO/contract owner and whether procurement requires a signed MSA before a pilot invoice can be issued? That will determine our order-of-operations.

Quick proposed sequence (we can flip per your needs):
- Week 1: Exchange redlines (MSA) + DPA review parallel
- Week 2: Legal alignment & sign MSA (or sign MSA w/ DPA SOW pending)
- Week 3: Order form + pricing/po issuance
- Week 4: Pilot onboarding + SOC2 evidence exchange

Attached: Novacare_MAP_v2.xlsx (MAP with owners & dates), and a copy of our standard MSA for reference.

If procurement needs a different cadence I can loop in Priyom to map acceptance criteria/technical gating into the MAP.

Thanks Ben / Sarah — looping in Laura (legal) and Rishi (infrastructure) to confirm sequencing and technical gates. Laura, primary legal asks from Novacare (per their redlines): indemnity cap tweaks, data residency note in the DPA, and a shorter SLA remedy window. Sarah / Ben — can you confirm if Novacare requires a specific DPA template or will your team accept our standard DPA with a few amendments?

I've drawn two runnable paths in the MAP:
- Path A (MSA-first): Sign MSA -> Sign Order Form -> Issue PO -> Onboard. 3 weeks if redlines are minor.
- Path B (Order-first): Sign Order Form referencing draft MSA -> Issue PO -> Onboard. Requires procurement flexibility; could compress to 10 business days but needs procurement sign-off (Ben noted internal finance deadline Oct 20).

For transparency I've highlighted these cells in Novacare_MAP_v2.xlsx: owners, decision gates, and fallback dates. If Oct 20 is a hard deadline we should aim for Path B and get an interim order form signed — legal can accept an LOI-style order form with agreed payment terms and a dependency clause for final MSA sign-off.

Attachment: Novacare_MAP_v2.xlsx (updated with Path A/B)

Marcus

Hi all — quick take from legal. Reviewed Ben's redlines. Two items we should close before any order-first approach:
1) DPA scope (data residency + processor/subprocessor list) — if Novacare requires explicit EU residency clauses we need to capture that now; otherwise a cross-reference to our DPA with an appendix is acceptable.
2) Indemnity/limitation language — Ben's edits increase Redwood exposure beyond our standard. If procurement insists on order-first I propose a short carve-out: a conditional escrowed liability cap for pilot usage, and a firm commit to finalize MSA within 30 days of PO.

Also, procurement ask: please provide SOC2 evidence. Rishi — can you pull the SOC2 snapshot and a link we can share? I'll prepare a one-page DPA addendum we can sign quickly for the pilot.

Laura Bennett
